gen-silkscreen-gf-ibm-plex-sans-thai-loo: IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped is a plain sans with curves that refuse to close. IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped gives lo-fi Silkscreen, with its spaced-out spaghetti lines, a clean counterweight that never fights back.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-linear-b: Retro to the core, Silkscreen leaves space around every letter, while Noto Sans Linear B stays modern and smooth. Silkscreen is best at lo-fi attitude; the body is best at smooth bends.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-mongolian: Silkscreen has a thickness like neon glass tubing, with room around every letter, paired with the flared terminals of Noto Sans Mongolian. Silkscreen does retro glow best; the body does modern text best.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoined: Silkscreen draws without any brush-like swelling, each letter spaced apart, while Noto Sans NKo Unjoined is an approachable sans-serif. Lo-fi spacing up top, wide openings below: that is the draw.
gen-silkscreen-gf-quattrocento-sans: Lo-fi, spaced-out and unmistakably retro, with a clean body below. Silkscreen does that spaghetti-line nostalgia best, while Quattrocento Sans does the quiet work of keeping c from looking like o.
gen-silkscreen-gf-roboto-flex: Signage-plain and lo-fi, Silkscreen leaves space around every letter, line weights all alike. And Roboto Flex, an approachable sans-serif with a wide slot in each c, takes over for the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-rosario: Spaced-out and lo-fi, with bowls that never thin at the sides. Silkscreen sets the retro tone up top, and Rosario, a plain sans with ends of the c that never turn inward, carries the text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ruluko: Retro, lo-fi letters whose round walls match the straight ones in weight. Silkscreen does spaced-out spaghetti nostalgia best, while Ruluko, a sans, handles approachable text with broad counters on c and s.
gen-silkscreen-gf-sansation: Approachable curves with no ink pooling where they turn inward. Silkscreen is best at lo-fi, retro lettering with no stroke modulation, while Sansation is best at smooth, neutral running text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varta: Lo-fi, retro, and spaced out like spaghetti. Silkscreen is best at diagonals that match its uprights in weight, while Varta, a plain sans, is best at big open eyes on every e and a.
